question: Which of the following observations best supports that liquids have a definite volume but no fixed shape?

options.text: Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume
Air expands to fill the entire container
A sponge changes its shape when squeezed
A solid iron block retains its shape in any container

solution:
The correct answer is __**Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Liquids have a definite volume:** Liquids maintain a consistent volume regardless of the container they are poured into. This property differentiates liquids from gases, which expand to occupy the entire volume of the container.
 
• **No fixed shape:** Liquids adapt to the shape of the container they are poured into. For instance, water poured into a cylindrical container takes on a cylindrical shape, while in a square container, it assumes a square shape.
 
• **Correct observation:** The statement "Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume" accurately highlights the defining characteristics of liquids. This observation demonstrates the ability of liquids to change shape while maintaining their volume.
 
• **Statement analysis:**
 
 
• Option 1: "Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume" – Correct. This accurately describes the behavior of liquids.
 
• Option 2: "Air expands to fill the entire container" – Incorrect. This describes the behavior of gases, not liquids.
